author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page when a page below the first is requested
summary: A request for the owner listing naming a page numbered below the first is treated as a request for the first page, and the normal listing is shown instead of an error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a last name search asking for a page numbered zero or below, when the search runs, then the first page of matches is listed rather than an error page
given an empty search asking for a page numbered zero or below, when it runs, then the first page of every owner is listed rather than an error page
given a listing asked for a page numbered below the first, when it is shown, then it reports itself as being on the first page, not on the number that was asked for
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's handling of a page below the first
a page value that is not a number
a page numbered beyond the last page of results
notes: Scope is bounded by the recorded intake at line 1, whose decisions array is empty. Two adjacent questions the request did not settle are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions and listed here as non-goals for this slice: the veterinarian directory, and a non-numeric page value. Requirement is stated by the owner, not derived; marked (stated 2026-08-14) in docs/prd.md. Edge case 4 of Owner records carries the reported-page criterion.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice sits entirely inside the existing feature-package shape (system-design.md Overview, Package Structure): OwnerController holds its own paging helper, with no service layer and no shared pagination abstraction. The adjustment is one normalization of the requested page at the web boundary. grep of OwnerController.java confirms the covering code still resolves as memory recalls it: the handler takes page as an int request parameter defaulting to 1 (line 95), passes it to findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (line 107) which builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) (line 135), and passes the same raw value to addPaginationModel as the currentPage model attribute (lines 121, 126). A page below 1 therefore asks PageRequest for a negative index, which rejects it, and the error page renders. No IDE oracle is connected in this run, so grep is the weaker basis for that resolution claim. No new package, type, pattern, or dependency; no ADR warranted.
integration_points: the Contracts row for OwnerController now carries REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 and states the below-first-page guarantee
the owners/ownersList template's paging links read the currentPage model attribute, which the normalized value feeds

patterns.description: normalize the requested page once, where it enters the handler, so the single normalized value feeds both the PageRequest and the currentPage model attribute. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries places validation at the boundary and keeps defensive checks out of the core; normalizing only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would stop the exception but leave currentPage reporting the number that was asked for, failing the third acceptance criterion
edge case 4 of Owner records is the reported-page criterion; the PRD contract is to clamp, not to reject, so the boundary rule here is normalization rather than the reject-what-is-not-allowed default

risks.risk: clamping below the zero-page boundary must not itself overflow: the most negative int reaches page - 1 only if normalization is skipped
risks.mitigation: normalize to a floor of the first page before any arithmetic on the value

risks.risk: VetController carries the identical page - 1 shape (VetController.java:45,62) and is left unfixed, so the two listings will diverge in behavior where today they merely duplicate structure
risks.mitigation: deliberate: the veterinarian directory is a declared non-goal of this slice and is recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md. Not a refactor-first case, since the slice lands cleanly without reshaping the ground; extracting a shared paging helper across two feature packages would breach the package independence recorded in system-design.md Package Structure and needs its own decision

risks.risk: a page beyond the last page returns an empty Page, and the empty branch reports the last name as not found
risks.mitigation: pre-existing behavior, declared a non-goal of this slice; do not change the empty-result branch

notes: Verdict is minor rather than covered because durable memory recorded no treatment of an out-of-range page parameter and the Contracts table's Implements mapping had no entry for this requirement. One edit landed in docs/system-design.md: the OwnerController row now names the guarantee and cites REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001. No Known Defects row was added, since that table records defects that remain in the code and this slice fixes this one. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Non-numeric page values remain out of scope: the int parameter binding rejects them upstream of the paging helper, a different failure path.

The explanatory comment states the why (boundary normalization, overflow avoidance, single value feeding both query and model) rather than restating the code, consistent with the file's existing // comment style

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain check did NOT run against the NVD: no OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access. Resolved framework versions from ./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath are Spring Boot 4.1.0, Spring Framework 7.0.8, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE (thymeleaf-spring6). Treat these as unverified against the NVD - a human or CI should close the check. The change itself adds and upgrades no dependency, so the supply-chain surface is unchanged by this slice.

Class sweep for the same shape across production code: grep -rn 'PageRequest.of' src/main/java finds one further instance, VetController.java:61 (PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)) with no clamp, so /vets.html?page=0 still throws and renders the error page with the underlying exception message. This is out of scope by declaration (PRD non-goal and an Open Question, design-block risk 2) and pre-existing, so it is not a finding on this change - but it is now the only remaining instance of the class, and the information-disclosure aspect (exception text on the error page) makes it worth its own slice.

Upper-bound page values (for example page=2147483647) are unclamped and unchanged by this slice: Spring Data computes the offset as a long, so no overflow occurs, but the resulting deep-offset query makes the database scan before returning an empty page. Pre-existing and declared a non-goal ('a page numbered beyond the last page of results'); noted for a future slice, not a defect in this change.
approved_aspects: Boundary validation placed correctly: the request-derived page is normalized once in processFindForm (OwnerController.java:103) before any arithmetic, matching security-principles.md Trust Boundaries ('validate at the boundary, defensive checks belong at the boundary, not scattered through the core'). The private helpers now receive an already-normalized value rather than re-checking it.

Integer-underflow path closed: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) clamps before the decrement, so Integer.MIN_VALUE can no longer wrap to a positive page index at PageRequest.of(currentPage - FIRST_PAGE, pageSize) (OwnerController.java:143). The parameterized tests cover 0, -1, and Integer.MIN_VALUE explicitly, so the overflow case is regression-guarded.

No injection surface introduced: the value stays a bound int end to end; data access remains the Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith with a Pageable, so no request-derived text reaches query construction (threat model row 'SQL injection' unchanged).

XSS/template safety unchanged and narrowed: owners/ownersList.html uses Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${currentPage - 1}__, __${currentPage + 1}__) on the currentPage model attribute. currentPage is an int, so no expression text can ride it; the clamp strictly narrows the reachable range to >= 1, leaving the template safer than the baseline, not weaker. Template files are unchanged by the diff.
No secrets, credentials, or sensitive values added. Grep over the diff for token/password/secret/key returns nothing; the only new constant is FIRST_PAGE = 1.

No new dangerous primitives: the diff adds no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec call, no file or path I/O, no deserialization config, no @JsonTypeInfo, no logging of request data, no System.out/err, and no java.util.Random. No system /tmp usage.

Error-handling posture improved: the change removes an IllegalArgumentException path that previously reached the error page (which renders the underlying exception message per system-design.md Known Defects), so an attacker-controllable page value no longer produces internal exception text for /owners.
No new endpoint, no widened management exposure, no mass-assignment surface (no new @InitBinder or request-bound type), no change to the dependency set - build.gradle is not in the change set.

Not a defect — the reported-page behavior runs through the same addPaginationModel code path already covered by theOwnerListingShouldReportTheFirstPageWhenTheRequestedPageIsBelowTheFirst — but adding a currentPage assertion there would make the PRD's named-search Done-when criterion directly self-verifying rather than inferred from a shared path.
approved_aspects: pagesBelowTheFirst() covers exactly the PRD's edge-case boundary set (0, -1, Integer.MIN_VALUE), with the MIN_VALUE inclusion explained by a WHY comment (decrement-overflow) rather than restating WHAT
New tests follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school and the host file's existing MockMvc + MockitoBean idiom (the sanctioned mock per testing-principles.md Mocking Policy)
Four-phase structure with blank-line separation, no phase comments, no mystery literals (BROADEST_SEARCH named constant, FIRST_PAGE constant mirrors production semantics)
New factories (anOwner(), aPageOfSeveralOwners()) wrap construction rather than calling constructors inline, consistent with Test Data Construction guidance
jacocoTestReport confirms full coverage (fc) of the new Math.max clamp line and the adjusted PageRequest.of arithmetic
./gradlew test passes clean; all three parameterized tests exercise the fix without invented data

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the requested owners page at the handler boundary

blast_radius.note: Four files in one module, 20 production lines confined to a single MVC handler and its two private paging helpers; no sensitive paths, no dependency or config change, and the two unknown-kind paths are docs/prd.md and docs/system-design.md rather than unclassified code.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the description says: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) runs before any arithmetic so Integer.MIN_VALUE cannot wrap at PageRequest.of(currentPage - FIRST_PAGE), and the page-to-currentPage renames in the private helpers are mechanical, with grep confirming the owners template consumes the same clamped currentPage attribute and no other caller passes the raw value.

test_adequacy.note: The three parameterized tests would fail against the pre-fix code, since page 0 reached PageRequest.of(-1) and rendered the error page; they assert real outcomes (HTTP 200, the ownersList view, the listed owners, and currentPage equal to 1) across 0, -1, and Integer.MIN_VALUE rather than restating the implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved on the first pass with empty findings lists; the security and test recommendations disclaim themselves as non-findings, covering declared non-goals (the unclamped VetController, upper-bound pages) and one optional extra assertion, and the un-run supply-chain check does not attach to a change that touches no dependency.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions; the touched files match the design-block's primary and supporting paths exactly, and the adjacent surfaces the fix could have wandered into are recorded as PRD non-goals and Open Questions instead of edited.

rationale: A one-line clamp placed before the arithmetic that caused the bug, with parameterized tests that fail against the old code and a clean first-pass roster. Confirm and merge.
